deep.reconstruction:
Problem: for every number of the form a²+1, list all its divisors smaller than a. Solution (a sieve):
1. Write out a = 1, 2, …, 2000, the range covered by the preceding table.
2. Every odd prime divisor of a²+1 has the form 4n+1. The preceding table gives, for each such prime p < 2000, the residue r with r² ≡ −1 (mod p). Then p | a²+1 exactly when a ≡ ±r (mod p).
3. Attach 2 to every odd a. Attach 5 to a ≡ ±2 (mod 5), 13 to a ≡ ±5 (mod 13), 17 to a ≡ ±4 (mod 17), and so on.
4. Skip the representatives a < p (that is, a = r and a = p − r), since only divisors below a are wanted.
5. Each a then carries exactly its prime divisors below a. The larger part of a²+1 follows by division.
Since a composite a²+1 must have a prime factor at most √(a²+1), hence at most a (and p = a is impossible for a > 1), an a that carries no mark gives a prime a²+1. The next page (Coroll. 1–3) draws exactly this conclusion. It is a sieve on the values of the polynomial x²+1, built from its roots modulo p, and serves Euler's aim of exhibiting primes well above 10⁵–10⁶.
errors: The Solution claims 'all divisors' of aa+1 below a are obtained, but only the prime divisors are attached, and their multiplicity is not recorded. Powers and composite divisors below a, and the exact cofactor, require further division. For example, a = 7 gives 50 = 2·5², and only 2 and 5 are marked.
The phrase 'formae 2m±1' is redundant: it just means odd a.

The neglect of multiplicity causes a real error on the next page (Coroll. 3: a single attached divisor α implies (aa+1)/α is prime). Counterexample: a = 32 gives 1025 = 5²·41. Only 5 is attached, since 32 is even and 41 > 32, yet 1025/5 = 205 is not prime.

ideas.what: Sieving the values a²+1 by primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4), using the two square roots of −1 mod p
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial sieve / sieve of Eratosthenes on polynomial values (a precursor of the quadratic sieve idea)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E283) for the a²+1 prime table; later extended by Cunningham and others
ideas.where_published: E283, Novi Commentarii 9 (1762/3, publ. 1764); also Euler's correspondence with Goldbach on primes of the form a²+1

ideas.what: Odd prime divisors of a²+1 are of the form 4n+1
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic character of −1 / divisors of sums of two coprime squares

ideas.what: If a²+1 has no prime divisor ≤ a, it is prime; at most one prime factor exceeds a

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known Euler sieve for primes of the form a²+1 in E283, already discussed in histories of the n²+1 problem (Landau's problem). There is nothing unrecorded here. The only notable point is the multiplicity oversight, which leads to an error in Coroll. 3 on the next page.
transcription_corrections: The printed text reads 'ipſa rdice/redice a' (a typographical slip for 'radice'); the transcription silently normalizes it to 'radice'.
